absent: Numeric values of cpuset flag bits and the full filetype enumeration.
Internals of scheduler domain construction and partition distribution.
Cgroup path formatting, css lookup and namespace semantics.
V1 validation routine delegated outside these fragments.
Memory migration, pressure metering and spread application details.
Deadline bandwidth structures and root domain accounting.
Housekeeping, isolated cpu and hotplug handling beyond flags seen.
Task attach and migration workqueue protocol beyond the progress counter.

findings.text: Public cpuset controls let callers test cpu exclusivity overlap between two sets, update a single flag through validated trial commit, and latch a scheduler domain rebuild request.
Global root state and v1 interface surface include the top set object, the v1 file table, initialization and online hooks, and proc display of a task set path with newline termination.

Synchronization and scheduler integration expose mutex lock and unlock wrappers with a held check, domain rebuild in several locking contexts, reset to defaults, and deadline task counting with accounting refresh.
Numeric v1 reads dispatch on the file private type to flag predicates, a global pressure enable, or a meter rate, treating unknown types as fatal.

Numeric v1 writes require an online set, serialize with the full lock, route flag types through the common flag updater, toggle the pressure enable directly, emit one time deprecation notices for legacy knobs, and reject unknown types.

Flag updates duplicate the set into a trial copy, toggle one bit, validate the trial, commit only the flag word under callback protection, then rebuild scheduling when balance changes on a non empty set and refresh spread state when that property changes.

Trial creation duplicates the base object or allocates a fresh zeroed one, sets deadline and linkage defaults, allocates four cpu mask objects with cleanup on partial failure, and copies mask contents when duplicating.

Change validation uses v1 checks outside v2 mode, exempts the root, refuses shrinking an exclusive balanced set that would strand deadline tasks, and refuses sibling overlap on cpu or memory exclusivity.

V1 cpu conflict means either side exclusive with intersecting allowed sets; v2 cpu conflict means intersecting exclusive sets with an added subset guard on change; memory conflict means either side exclusive with intersecting node sets.
Effective cpu and memory sets intersect the requested set with the parent effective set, falling back to the parent set when empty in v2 mode.

Placement guarantee starts from possible intersect active cpus, ascends ancestors for an intersecting effective set, and falls back to filtered active cpus on hotplug race; population considers direct tasks and non partition descendants while skipping an excluded child.

Online handling inherits spread properties from the parent and, when clone children is set, refuses cloning if any sibling is exclusive and otherwise copies parent memory and cpu state under callback protection.

Temporary mask bundles allocate and release three masks together with null tolerance; deadline refresh skips sets without deadline tasks or with empty effective sets, clears per cpu visited marks, and iterates remaining sets with temporary references.

Hierarchy walks hold read side RCU protection, including proc display combined with css set spin protection, plus validation, population, guarantee and deadline traversal with temporary references across unlocks.

Flag words commit under the callback spinlock with interrupts disabled; v1 writes and rebuild paths use the main cpuset mutex, some with added cpu read protection, and deadline rebuild asserts cpuset, cpu and domain mutex holdings.
Attach serialization centers on an in progress counter under the main mutex with a wait queue; waiters loop acquiring the mutex until idle, and completions wake waiters when the counter reaches zero.
Temporary mask bundle groups three cpu masks for partition deltas and hierarchy recomputation; the array allocator builds caller supplied pointer arrays and unwinds earlier successes on failure.
Attach context is one static record with a progress count, update flags for cpus, memory, work and multi destination cases, a source set pointer, and a destination node mask.

Root set starts exclusive on cpu and memory with load balancing enabled, marked as partition root with deadline ownership cleared; observed set state spans flags, several cpu and node masks, meters, partition and error markers, deadline counts and linkage.
Module state includes static branch switches, top and general mutexes, a callback spinlock, housekeeping and rebuild flags, a v2 mode flag, several global cpu masks, and a migration workqueue.

Partition roles use member zero, root one, isolated two, with invalid variants as negative mirrors; invalidation negates positives only, membership and invalidity have dedicated tests, and changes notify files while clearing errors on return to valid.

Mode state treats v2 as active when compiled for v2 or the runtime flag is set; rebuild requests latch a boolean; partition failures index a diagnostic table; insane memory configuration latches a global switch once.

External entries are proc display emitting a path plus newline, the v1 file table binding list and numeric handlers to names, online and init callbacks, and lock plus rebuild helpers for core callers.

Errors include allocation exhaustion, offline sets, invalid sibling overlap, busy deadline shrink, oversized paths reported as overlong names, fatal trap on unknown numeric types, and warnings on empty placement intersections.

Legacy v1 knobs emit one time deprecation notices pointing to successors; movable only node sets latch an insane configuration warning; top set hotplug races can briefly leave no intersecting active cpu.
Partition codes are member 0, root 1, isolated 2, invalid root -1, invalid isolated -2.

V1 surface provides cpus, mems, effective cpus, effective mems, exclusivity, hardwall, load balance, relax level, migrate, pressure, page spread, slab spread, and a root only pressure enable; list writes allow base one hundred plus six per cpu or node.
